technical_and_design_decisions: For Python processor integration, adopt a stdin/stdout subprocess execution model instead of native JNI integration, to avoid platform-specific native dependencies, simplify deployment in cloud/containerized environments, and align with Spring XD's support for external process-based modules.

For R processor integration, use the Renjin JVM-based R implementation instead of rJava, to eliminate the requirement for a local R runtime installation, reduce deployment complexity, and ensure compatibility with JVM-based Spring XD containers.

For Hive sink implementation, leverage the official Spring for Apache Hive integration library to handle Hive connectivity and data writing operations, rather than building custom Hive client logic, to reduce development effort and improve reliability.

For access control list (ACL) implementation for DSL Shell and Admin UI, use Spring Security's ACL module as the underlying framework, to reuse mature, well-tested ACL logic and avoid building custom access control infrastructure from scratch.

For administration endpoint security, use Spring Boot's built-in SSL configuration support and native Spring Security Basic Auth integration, rather than implementing custom security logic, to reduce development effort and align with Spring best practices.

For REST API entity-specific role-based access control, use Spring Security's method-level security annotations to enforce access policies, integrated with the shared ACL infrastructure, to ensure consistent access control across all application components.

The development team has existing proficiency with Spring Framework, Spring Security, Spring XD module development, and the selected third-party libraries, so no additional training or learning effort is required.

Test environments for Python, R, and Apache Hive are pre-provisioned, accessible, and properly configured for integration testing, with no environment setup effort included in the development estimates.

Default ACL permission requirements (all authenticated users can view streams, only users with stream-write/admin role can create/destroy streams) are finalized and do not require additional stakeholder review or adjustment during development.

SSL keystore and certificate provisioning for administration endpoints is managed by the operations team, so development work only covers configuration support and does not include certificate generation or infrastructure setup.
